title: Fortidsvaner med pleide å — past habits
goal: Use pleide å for recurring past behavior, not one finished event.

objectives.statement: Use pleide å for recurring past behavior, not one finished event.

spans.value: Maja has recently returned to the town where she grew up. She meets her childhood friend Jonas near the river.
Da jeg bodde her, pleide jeg å sykle langs elva hver morgen.

blocks.translation: When I lived here, I used to cycle along the river every morning.

spans.value: Ja, og du pleide å vente på meg ved den gamle brua.

blocks.translation: Yes, and you used to wait for me by the old bridge.

spans.value: Vi pleide å kjøpe is i kiosken etter skolen også.

blocks.translation: We used to buy ice cream at the kiosk after school too.

spans.value: Det stemmer. Eieren pleide å kjenne alle barna i området.

blocks.translation: That’s right. The owner used to know all the children in the area.

spans.value: I går syklet jeg langs elva igjen.

blocks.translation: Yesterday I cycled along the river again.
Did you stop at the kiosk?

spans.value: Ja, jeg kjøpte en is. Men den gamle eieren jobber ikke der nå.

blocks.translation: Yes, I bought an ice cream. But the old owner doesn’t work there now.

spans.value: Maja and Jonas talk about two kinds of past experience. First, they remember routines from their childhood: cycling by the river, waiting at the bridge, and buying ice cream after school. These things happened regularly over a period of time. Then Maja describes what she did yesterday: she cycled, stopped, and bought one ice cream on one finished occasion.
That difference is the focus of this chapter.

sections.title: Saying what someone used to do

spans.value: when you want to present an action as a recurring past behavior or old routine.

no.value: Maja pleide å sykle langs elva.

en.value: Maja used to cycle along the river.

items.value: pleide places the routine in the past.
sykle is the infinitive (infinitiv), the basic verb form.

spans.value: The same pattern works with different subjects:

no.value: Jeg pleide å gå til skolen.

en.value: I used to walk to school.

no.value: Han pleide å lage middag på søndager.

en.value: He used to make dinner on Sundays.

no.value: Vi pleide å besøke bestemor hver sommer.

en.value: We used to visit Grandma every summer.

no.value: Barna pleide å leke ute etter skolen.

en.value: The children used to play outside after school.

spans.value: does not change with the subject:

no.value: Jeg pleide å lese før jeg la meg.

en.value: I used to read before going to bed.

no.value: De pleide å lese før de la seg.

en.value: They used to read before going to bed.

statement.value: Use pleide å + infinitive to describe something that happened regularly during a past period.

spans.value: Words and phrases such as these often support that meaning:

items.value: da jeg var liten — when I was little

spans.value: These expressions do not create the grammar by themselves, but they help establish a recurring situation.

no.value: Da jeg var liten, pleide jeg å besøke tante Liv hver sommer.

en.value: When I was little, I used to visit Aunt Liv every summer.

no.value: Før pleide Amir å ta bussen til jobb.

en.value: Amir used to take the bus to work before.

no.value: Vi pleide å spise sammen på fredager.

en.value: We used to eat together on Fridays.

sections.title: A routine, not one finished event
A repeated journey and one completed journey

no.value: Før pleide Nora å gå til jobb.

en.value: Nora used to walk to work before.

no.value: I går gikk Nora til jobb.

en.value: Yesterday Nora walked to work.

spans.value: The first sentence describes Nora’s former routine. The second reports one completed journey yesterday.

no.value: Vi pleide å besøke bestemor hver søndag.

en.value: We used to visit Grandma every Sunday.

no.value: Vi besøkte bestemor på søndag.

en.value: We visited Grandma on Sunday.

spans.value: . The single Sunday visit is expressed with the ordinary past tense (preteritum), which you already know.

sections.title: A former evening habit and one evening

no.value: Erik pleide å lese før han la seg.

en.value: Erik used to read before going to bed.

no.value: Erik leste ferdig boka i går kveld.

en.value: Erik finished the book last night.

spans.value: The first sentence presents reading as Erik’s routine. The second tells us about one finished event.
The important question is not simply, Did this happen in the past? Both forms refer to the past. Ask instead:

statement.value: Am I presenting this as a regular behavior over a past period, or as one finished event?

spans.value: for the regular behavior. Do not use it merely because a sentence contains a past-time expression.

no.value: I fjor pleide vi å dra på hytta hver helg.

en.value: Last year we used to go to the cabin every weekend.

no.value: I fjor dro vi på hytta én gang.

en.value: Last year we went to the cabin once.

spans.value: , but only the first describes a habit.

sections.title: More than once does not always mean a habit

spans.value: A habit is a repeated behavior connected to a period or routine. An action can happen several times during one finished occasion without becoming a habit.

no.value: Da jeg studerte, pleide jeg å ringe mamma hver søndag.

en.value: When I was a student, I used to call Mum every Sunday.

no.value: I går ringte jeg mamma tre ganger.

en.value: Yesterday I called Mum three times.

spans.value: Three calls are more than one call, but they all belong to one finished day. The second sentence does not describe an established routine.

no.value: Sara pleide å kjøpe kaffe på vei til jobb.

en.value: Sara used to buy coffee on her way to work.

no.value: I morges kjøpte Sara to kopper kaffe.

en.value: This morning Sara bought two cups of coffee.

spans.value: Two cups do not make the event a past habit. The time frame is one particular morning.

sections.title: Keep the next verb in the infinitive

spans.value: , use the infinitive. Do not put the second verb in the past tense.

no.value: Hun pleide å gå hjem etter skolen.

en.value: She used to walk home after school.

no.value: Hun pleide å gikk hjem etter skolen.

en.value: 'Incorrect: She used to walked home after school.'

spans.value: The past meaning is already carried by

no.value: Vi pleide å spise middag klokka fem.

en.value: We used to eat dinner at five o’clock.

no.value: Vi pleide spiste middag klokka fem.

en.value: 'Incorrect: We used ate dinner at five o’clock.'

no.value: Jonas pleide å vente ved brua.

en.value: Jonas used to wait by the bridge.

no.value: Jonas pleide vente ved brua.

en.value: 'Incorrect: Jonas used to wait by the bridge.'

spans.value: For this lesson, remember the construction as one unit:
often suggests that the old routine has changed or ended. Context usually makes this clearer.

no.value: Før pleide jeg å ta toget til jobb, men nå jobber jeg hjemme.

en.value: I used to take the train to work, but now I work from home.

no.value: Lea pleide å spille håndball, men nå spiller hun fotball.

en.value: Lea used to play handball, but now she plays football.

no.value: Vi pleide å møtes hver fredag. Nå bor vi i forskjellige byer.

en.value: We used to meet every Friday. Now we live in different cities.

spans.value: The essential meaning remains recurring past behavior. A contrast with the present can make the old-routine meaning especially natural, but you do not need to add a present-day contrast every time.

no.value: Bestefar pleide å fortelle morsomme historier.

en.value: Grandpa used to tell funny stories.

spans.value: This is complete even without a sentence about the present.
After their walk, Maja and Jonas sit outside the old kiosk.

blocks.translation: Do you remember the park behind the school?

spans.value: Ja. Vi pleide å spille fotball der etter skolen.

blocks.translation: Yes. We used to play football there after school.

spans.value: Og du pleide å ta med appelsiner til alle.

blocks.translation: And you used to bring oranges for everyone.

spans.value: Det gjorde jeg! I går gikk jeg gjennom parken, men ingen spilte fotball.

blocks.translation: I did! Yesterday I walked through the park, but nobody was playing football.

spans.value: The old football games and the oranges were part of a repeated routine. Maja’s walk yesterday was one finished event. The same contrast from the opening dialogue still applies.
Using pleide å for one dated event

no.value: I går pleide jeg å møte Jonas på kafeen.

en.value: 'Not: Yesterday I used to meet Jonas at the café. (for the intended meaning)'

spans.value: If there was one meeting yesterday, use a finished past event:

no.value: I går møtte jeg Jonas på kafeen.

en.value: Yesterday I met Jonas at the café.

spans.value: only if meeting Jonas was a recurring past practice:

no.value: Før pleide jeg å møte Jonas på kafeen hver torsdag.

en.value: I used to meet Jonas at the café every Thursday.

no.value: Vi pleide å kjøpte is etter skolen.

en.value: 'Incorrect: We used to bought ice cream after school.'

no.value: Vi pleide å kjøpe is etter skolen.

en.value: We used to buy ice cream after school.

spans.value: can introduce either a routine or a finished event.

no.value: I fjor pleide jeg å svømme hver morgen.

en.value: Last year I used to swim every morning.

no.value: I fjor svømte jeg over fjorden én gang.

en.value: Last year I swam across the fjord once.

spans.value: Read the whole situation. Look for recurring behavior, not merely a reference to the past.
Imagine that Henrik has returned to the neighborhood where he lived while studying. He wants to explain his old weekday routine and then report one thing he did during today’s visit.

prompt.value: Choose the complete interpretation of the supplied Maja and Jonas statements that separates recurring childhood routines from actions during Maja's single trip yesterday and identifies the helpful time expressions.

options.text: The four lines with «pleide å» describe one finished event, while the lines connected to «I går» describe routines. «I går» names a recurring past period.
options.why: «Pleide å» marks recurring past behavior, and «I går» places an action in a finished past time.

options.text: Only «hver morgen» marks a routine. «Da jeg bodde her» and «etter skolen» describe single events, while the three actions connected to «I går» are routines.
options.why: The context presents «Da jeg bodde her» and «etter skolen» as part of repeated childhood routines, not single events.

options.text: The recurring childhood routines are «Da jeg bodde her, pleide jeg å sykle langs elva hver morgen.» (When I lived here, I used to cycle along the river every morning), «Ja, og du pleide å vente på meg ved den gamle brua.» (Yes, and you used to wait for me by the old bridge), «Vi pleide å kjøpe is i kiosken etter skolen også.» (We used to buy ice cream at the kiosk after school too), and «Det stemmer. Eieren pleide å kjenne alle barna i området.» (That’s right. The owner used to know all the children in the area.). The single trip yesterday includes «I går syklet jeg langs elva igjen.» (Yesterday I cycled along the river again), «Stoppet du ved kiosken?» (Did you stop at the kiosk?), and «Ja, jeg kjøpte en is.» (Yes, I bought an ice cream). «Da jeg bodde her», «hver morgen», and «etter skolen» support a recurring past period, while «I går» places actions in one finished trip.
options.why: This separates recurring past behavior from actions in one finished visit and uses the conversation’s time expressions as evidence.

options.text: All seven actions belong to recurring childhood behavior because several actions occurred. The distinction between «pleide å» and ordinary past forms does not matter.
options.why: Several actions during one visit do not become a recurring past habit.

stem.value: Which interpretation correctly separates the recurring routines from the finished trip?

prompt.value: A former routine: We regularly read together at weekends. Build one complete Norwegian sentence using subject + pleide å + infinitive.

Sara regularly bought coffee on her way to work in the past. This morning she bought two cups. Choose the pair that uses pleide å only for the former recurring behavior and ordinary past for today's finished action.

options.text: «Sara kjøpte kaffe på vei til jobb. I morges kjøpte Sara to kopper kaffe.» (Sara bought coffee on her way to work. This morning Sara bought two cups of coffee.)
options.why: The first situation is a recurring former behavior, so the taught pattern uses pleide å.

options.text: «Sara pleide å kjøpe kaffe på vei til jobb. I morges kjøpte Sara to kopper kaffe.» (Sara used to buy coffee on her way to work. This morning Sara bought two cups of coffee.)
options.why: The first sentence presents a former routine with pleide å, while the second presents one finished action with ordinary past.

stem.value: Which pair completes both situations with the correct meaning?

prompt.value: Situation: I called Mum three times yesterday, during one finished day. Build the Norwegian sentence that presents this as one finished occasion rather than an established routine.
Find the one incorrect token in this sentence about a former routine and identify its taught repair. The error is inside pleide å + infinitive.

payload.feedback: Replace «gikk» with the infinitive «gå» after «å». «Pleide» already carries the past meaning.

prompt.value: Build a short continuation of Maja and Jonas's conversation. Include two old routines and one action from Maja's finished visit yesterday. Use pleide å + infinitive for routines and an ordinary past form for the visit.

Henrik has returned to the neighborhood where he lived as a student. Write 5–7 short Norwegian sentences about his regular travel, meals, study, and evening activities during his student years, using pleide å + infinitive for each recurring habit. Report one completed action during today's visit with an ordinary past-tense verb. Then briefly explain in Norwegian why pleide å fits the routine sentences but not today's finished event. Use your own wording; do not copy a complete sentence from the lesson.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against the task and report evidence for each criterion. Accept natural Bokmål variants and suitable ordinary past-tense verbs; do not require exact wording from the lesson.

criteria.instruction: Describes Henrik's regular travel, meals, study, and evening activities with pleide å + infinitive.
Reports one completed action during today's visit with an ordinary past-tense verb, not pleide å.
Briefly explains in Norwegian why pleide å fits recurring past behavior but not one finished event.
Uses Henrik's new situation and own wording instead of copying a complete sentence from the lesson.
